text:
maria: Weird one this morning — after updating to redwoodctl 0.18, my zsh login hook hangs during `local-serve` startup on my macbook. it looks like the CLI is trying to open a browser during the hook and blocks the dev terminal.

lee: is this the shell hook that auto-refreshes tokens? we added a check recently that runs `redwoodctl whoami` if no token cached.

maria: yes. i have an interactive terminal, but the login falls into the browser-open path which tries `open` and waits. i usually expect a device-code fallback for headless boxes, but on mac it preferred browser.

patrick: hmm. we should never block a shell hook waiting for browser. the hook should prefer non-blocking checks and only bail with a gentle message. can you paste your hook snippet?

maria: sure:

```
# in ~/.zshrc
if type redwoodctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  redwoodctl auth-refresh --quiet || redwoodctl login
fi
```

maria: when auth-refresh fails it runs `redwoodctl login` which triggers browser open.

lee: that `login` call is too eager for a shell startup. recommend replacing with `redwoodctl login --device` in hooks or using REDWOODCTL_SKIP_AUTOLOGIN=1 during interactive sessions.

maria: i also noticed that on CI our flaky auth retries are causing false-positive failures. GH actions job runs `redwoodctl login --token $REDWOOD_API_KEY` but sometimes the `redwoodctl` process exits with code 2 with no stdout due to a transient network dial timeout, and our workflow treats that as fatal.

ci-bot: Note: CI retry policy currently retries the whole job, not the login step. See docs: https://internal.example.com/ci/retry-policy

patrick: we need clearer exit codes from redwoodctl for auth vs transient network vs config errors. then CI can handle retries only for network-related exits.

lee: small proposal: exit code 10 = auth failure (bad token/permissions), 11 = network transient (timeout, DNS), 12 = config error (malformed profiles). Logging should include a one-line machine-readable hint.

maria: also a UX thing: when local-serve spawns `redwoodctl login`, it doesn't pass through env vars like REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR so we end up hitting different profile stores and then the token isn't found. i had a case where local-serve created a per-project .redwood while my hook used ~/.redwood and they diverged.

patrick: oof. local-serve should inherit environment passed to the parent process or accept `--config-dir` flag to be explicit. open a PR?

lee: opened PDE-501: local-serve should surface `--config-dir` and preserve env when spawning subcommands. assigned to eng-platform.

maria: in the meantime, my workaround was to set `export REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.redwood` in my zshrc before the hook and change the hook to `redwoodctl auth-refresh --no-block`. also replaced `redwoodctl login` with `redwoodctl login --device --no-open` so it prints a device URL if needed.

maria: snippet i used:

```
# ~/.zshrc
export REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.redwood
if type redwoodctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  redwoodctl auth-refresh --no-block || redwoodctl login --device --no-open || true
fi
```

lee: nice. consider using `--no-open` as the default for CI and shell hooks. we should add a note to the CLI install docs.

patrick: also worth adding a quick lint in `redwoodctl config` to detect multiple profile stores (e.g., ~/.redwood vs ./.redwood) and warn at startup. that would have surfaced the mismatch.

devex-bot: Feature request filed: PDE-512 add config-dir flag to local-serve, make login non-blocking in shell hooks, and implement exit-code taxonomy.

maria: one last thing — sample-app quickstart uses `npm run dev` which spawns local-serve; the README currently suggests adding auth to PATH but doesn't mention REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR. i filed a tiny docs PR to add a short troubleshooting section.

lee: sweet. CI team can also add a step: `redwoodctl --version || (echo 'redwoodctl missing or quarantined' && exit 1)` before running login, to fail fast and give a clearer reason.

patrick: agreed. i'll add tests in our e2e matrix: mac zsh login hook and GH actions login retry behavior. let's track flaky login failures and ensure we only retry on network exit codes.

maria: thanks all — this explains the morning confusion. will update my PR with the hook snippet and point to PDE-512. closing when docs + CLI changes land. :sparkles:
